title: Love is my vocation (Story of a Soul)
hook: searching for her place, Thérèse finds it: in the heart of the church, I will be love
tomorrow: calm inside first, or fix the room first? two old answers.

segments.voice: Yesterday Thérèse was too small for the stairs, and found a lift: his arms are the lift. Today she has the opposite problem. Too many dreams.
screen: `HIS ARMS ARE THE LIFT.` → `TOO MANY DREAMS.`

segments.voice: Every other post is a plan: the major, the city, the five-year path. Thérèse wants all of them. Warrior, priest, apostle, teacher, martyr. She wants to preach in every part of the world, until the end of time. And she's a nun inside convent walls. So she opens Paul's letters, looking for her place. Here's the odd part: she finds it in a chapter that isn't about callings at all.
screen: `EVERYONE POSTING THE PLAN.` → `SHE WANTS EVERY CALLING.` → `THE ANSWER'S IN THE WRONG CHAPTER.`

segments.voice: First she reads 1 Corinthians 12, the chapter that should answer her. Paul says the church is one body with many members: apostles, prophets, teachers. It's a list of parts. She doesn't find herself on it. Not an eye, not a hand. So she keeps reading, past the end of the chapter, and that's the first clue. Paul says, “covet earnestly the best gifts: and yet shew I unto you a more excellent way.” The more excellent way is the next chapter: love. Without it, the greatest gifts are noise. Second clue: if the church is a body, she reasons, it must have a heart, and that heart burns with love. Love is what moves every member. Without it, she says, apostles would stop preaching and martyrs would refuse to shed their blood. So the puzzle solves itself. The list names the parts. She needed what moves all of them. And she writes the words this lesson is named for: my vocation is love. In the heart of the church, my mother, I will be love. And so, she says, I'll be everything. One more thing to tell a friend: her days didn't change. Same convent, same work, same sisters. What changed was where she stood inside them. Paul ends the chapter: “And now abideth faith, hope, charity, these three; but the greatest of these is charity.”
screen: `NOT ON PAUL'S LIST.` · `A MORE EXCELLENT WAY.` · `A BODY NEEDS A HEART.` · `SAME DAYS, NEW PLACE.` · then, large: `I WILL BE LOVE.`

segments.voice: Choose one place you'll be later today: a desk, a kitchen, a practice, a room with someone who isn't easy. Name what love would look like there, what's most likely to get in the way, and one small move for when it does. Then rest in that plan for the rest of the sit.
Love is my vocation. Thérèse's discovery: her calling was to be love, at the heart of the church.
Keep this one: I will be love. She didn't change places; she changed where she stood. See you tomorrow.

howItsDone: Readers of Story of a Soul return to this passage when they wonder where they fit; Thérèse read it as a call to live ordinary days with love at the center.

chat.says: everyone's posting majors. Nia's doing nursing. i still don't know what i'm FOR.
options: Thérèse didn't find a job title first. She found love, and it fit anywhere she was.
Pick the biggest calling you can. Thérèse wanted to be everything at once.

chat.meaning: Thérèse found no place on Paul's list of parts, then found love at the heart of the body. Her vocation was love, wherever she was.

Thérèse.meaning: Thérèse of Lisieux, a French Carmelite nun and saint

vocation.meaning: a calling: what a person's life is for

Corinthians.meaning: Paul's letters to the church in Corinth

charity.meaning: the King James word for love in 1 Corinthians 13

martyr.meaning: someone who dies rather than give up their faith
